title: Finite normal covering models over point blowups dominate any normal model
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian excellent regular local ring of dimension $2$, let $K=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$, let $L/K$ be a finite field extension, and let $B$ be the integral closure of $A$ in $L$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], [def-exc-excellent-ring], [def-weil-regular-scheme], [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], [def-pc-field-extension], [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. For every normal modification $a:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ (a proper morphism with $Y$ normal integral and function field $L$ inducing the identity on $L$), there is a finite sequence $X=X_n\to\cdots\to X_0=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of blowups at reduced closed points lying over $\mathfrak m$, possibly of length zero, such that the normalization $Z$ of $X$ in $L$ has a proper birational morphism $h:Z\to Y$ over $\operatorname{Spec}B$ inducing the identity on $L$ [def-nagata-global-blowup], [def-weil-closed-immersion], [def-fin-normalization-extension], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-pc-integral-scheme]. The scheme $X$ is regular, normal, integral, excellent and Noetherian of dimension $2$, and $q:Z\to X$ is finite with $Z$ normal integral and Noetherian of dimension $2$ [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism].
